palette.notes: NOT PIXEL ART (photo of Hama bead craft). Code's 37 colours/one ramp measure the red-lit photo, not a sprite palette. Whole frame bathed in red light; teal/black jacket and brown hair on the bead figure.

lighting: Single red practical light (Stranger Things Upside Down mood) floods the room; heavy vignette darkens the corners so the bead figure in the centre reads.
silhouette: Flat bead-sprite girl (front and back sides beaded) standing on a bead Demogorgon flower, framed by a bead vine arch; edge-on she becomes a thin sliver.

motion.timing: Code: median hold 33.3 ms, 17.89 changes/s at 576x1024 (a 30 fps camera clip). A hand flicks the figure and it spins on its pin: front, edge, back, edge, front, slowing to edge-on at the end.

texture: Real fused beads: round pixel cells with gaps and plastic shine; camera blur and compression soften it.
camera: Static handheld-on-tripod close-up, vertical; no cuts.

acting.enters: A finger flicks the figure into motion at the start.
acting.acts: The flat sprite spins, alternating face, edge (almost vanishes) and back, so the figure seems to turn around in place.
acting.exits: Ends edge-on, nearly invisible, as if she left.
acting.depth: Figure stands on the flower in front of the arch; arch and flower frame her as a little stage.

techniques: two-sided flat sprite spun on a pin: edge-on frame as a free disappear
coloured practical light for a whole-scene mood
vignette to frame a small centred subject
physical bead craft as pixel art presented in the real world
feel: NOT PIXEL ART: Hama bead craft photo; red room light + flat sprite spinning edge-on = spooky disappear-reappear loop
for_fred: Fake a turn by flipping Fred's sprite through a 1-2 px edge-on frame: he can vanish edge-on, then reappear facing the other way; cheap way to exit and come back without leaving the frame.
